question.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}]x(t)+\overset{f(t)}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}4{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]}},\,Φ=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3{e}^{2t} \\ {e}^{-4t} & -{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations and the fundamental matrix of the corresponding homogeneous system above. Using the method of variation of parameters, compute ${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)$ and the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t)$ of the system.
${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,,\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)={e}^{t}\,\,$ {{field-2}}
$\frac{4}{3}{e}^{-t}$ $\frac{9}{5}$
question.worked_solution:
We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3{e}^{2t} \\ {e}^{-4t} & -{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}4{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{0\cdot (-{e}^{2t})-3{e}^{2t}\cdot {e}^{-4t}}[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{2t} & -3{e}^{2t} \\ -{e}^{-4t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{2t}}{3}[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{2t} & -3{e}^{2t} \\ -{e}^{-4t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{4t} & {e}^{4t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-2t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{4t} & {e}^{4t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-2t} & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{3}{e}^{5t} \\ \frac{4}{3}{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{3}{e}^{5t} \\ \frac{4}{3}{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int \frac{7}{3}{e}^{5t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int \frac{4}{3}{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{15}{e}^{5t} \\ -\frac{4}{3}{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3{e}^{2t} \\ {e}^{-4t} & -{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{15}{e}^{5t} \\ -\frac{4}{3}{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4{e}^{t} \\ \frac{9}{5}{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={e}^{t}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ \frac{9}{5}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
